title: Collapse an empty carton flat on the stack of knocked-down cartons it lies on
instruction: Collapse the empty carton flat where it lies on the stack, and leave the stack in place.
context: Stockers and order fillers (SOC 53-7065, about 2.8 million US jobs, BLS) empty cartons all shift and break each one down for the cardboard bay or baler: the tape is slit, the flaps are opened out, and the carton is racked over along its creases until it lies flat with its flaps out straight, and it goes on the stack of flats. A carton left standing takes the room of the whole backroom; one forced across the wrong creases tears and springs open, so the stack leans and slides. The same rack-over is how most households break down a delivery box for the recycling bin, so the act is familiar on sight. The trial starts once the tape is slit (the knife step is its own act, left out for safety), the far end's flaps hanging loose as slitting left them. Done by a robot, it is a judgement in force: push the carton over along its own creases (not across them), stop before the stack moves, and fold the loose flaps out without dragging the flat.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is z = 0. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up; arm bases at y +30.5 cm and -30.5 cm. (1) Stack, loose: three knocked-down cartons, each 508 (y) x 356 (x) x 6.4 mm (a 12 x 8 x 6 in carton flat with its flaps out straight, two layers of 3.2 mm board), 0.20 kg each, centred x 270 mm, y 0, on a fixed brown board 540 x 380 x 3 mm; the stack's top is 22.2 mm up. Friction 0.5 board on board (est). (2) Carton, loose: an empty brown regular slotted carton (RSC), 12 x 8 x 6 in (305 x 203 x 152 mm), single-wall C-flute, 0.20 kg in all (0.55 kg per square metre of board). It lies on the stack's top on one long side with its open ends along x, so it stands as a four-panel sleeve 203 mm tall: two long panels (305 x 152 mm) underneath and on top, two short panels (203 x 152 mm) at its ends, 3.2 mm plates. The underneath panel spans y -254 to +51 mm at x 270 mm, so the -y end panel stands at the stack's -y end. Flaps: each panel has a 102 mm deep flap (4 in, half the 8 in width, as on every RSC) at each open end, eight in all: four 305 x 102 mm on the long panels, four 203 x 102 mm on the end panels. The carton was emptied through its near (-x) end, whose four flaps were folded back then and lie out straight, in line with their panels. Its far (+x) end's tape has just been slit along the seam (the knife step is its own act, left out for safety), so those four flaps hang loose at uneven angles, as a slit end's flaps do: the top panel's droops 45 degrees below level over the opening, the underneath panel's stands 30 degrees up off the stack, the -y end panel's hangs 30 degrees out past straight and the +y end panel's is straight (real trial: 40 to 55, 20 to 40, 20 to 40 and 0 to 10 degrees). The carton spans x 92 to 448 mm. The four corners are creases: rotating joints about axes along x, each held by 0.01 N m of friction and stopped about 97 degrees either side of square. The manufacturer's glue joint is the one at the -y end: a 38 mm tab creased on the end panel's edge and glued flat to the underneath panel, so the sleeve is a closed loop with one degree of freedom. Each flap is a rigid plate on its own crease along its panel's edge, sprung toward its set (where it rests, at first its start angle) at 0.3 N m per radian (est); bent more than 3 degrees from its set, the crease takes a new set where the flap is, as scored board does, so a flap stays where it is put; it turns about 97 degrees either side of straight. Panels and flaps pass through one another in the model (the carton still collides with the stack and the grippers), so the crease angles, not contact, say how folded it is (a raised bottom flap shows through the top layer's flaps, which on a real carton rest on it; the press that folds it down folds both). Racking the sleeve toward +y by pushing the -y end panel turns all four corner creases together; that end panel's loose flap turns up with it, and as the top panel comes down the stack's top folds its drooping flap out. Fully racked with every flap out straight it is two layers, 6.4 mm thick, 516 mm long and 356 mm wide with its flaps out, lying along the stack like the flats under it. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: End state, read at the last step from the poses of the carton's four panels and eight flaps, its crease angles, the three flats of the stack, and both grippers. Flat: every corner crease within 15 degrees of fully shut (interior angle 0) or fully open (180), and every flap within 15 degrees of straight out (in line with its panel); the carton's thickness (highest point over lowest, flaps included) 12 mm or less; its footprint within 540 mm (y) x 380 mm (x). On the stack: the footprint's centre within 60 mm of the stack's centre (top view) and the carton's lowest point within 6 mm of the stack's top. Offset: the same within 120 mm and 20 mm. Stack kept: no flat moved over 15 mm (top view) or 4 mm up, or turned over 8 degrees. Hands off: on every step of the last 1 s both grippers' fingers are 30 mm or more from the carton and every flat. Still: over the last 1 s no panel, flap or flat moves 5 mm or more or turns 5 degrees or more (no visible motion). Score 0 if any flat moved over 40 mm or turned over 30 degrees at any step, and 0 unless hands off and still. Otherwise: 1.0 flat, on the stack, stack kept; 0.75 flat, offset, stack kept; 0.5 flat anywhere else (or stack moved 15 to 40 mm); 0.25 not flat but 110 mm tall or less; 0 otherwise. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. Success: 1.0 held for 1 s. Real trial, per condition: flat, an angle gauge at each corner and flap crease, a straight rule across the top and a 12 mm block, a tape for the footprint; on the stack, a rule and a straight edge across the stack; stack kept, a pencil mark and a rule; hands off, a 30 mm spacer and the video; still, no visible motion of the carton or the stack over the final 1 s in both the top video (the station's overhead camera, looking down on the stack) and the side video (a camera on the far side of the table, 1 m from the stack at the height of its top, looking along -x at the carton's full length).
reset_notes: Lay the three flats, flaps out, on the board, centred, edges square. Lay the carton on its long side on top, glue tab at the -y end, underneath panel from y -254 to +51 mm, creases square. Near (-x) end: fold each flap back hard once and let it lie out straight (within 10 degrees). Far (+x) end: slit the tape along the seam (a fresh carton) and leave its flaps loose at the angles in the setup (check with an angle gauge). Replace a carton whose creases have gone limp; cartons are single use after about five trials.
fidelity: Rigid 3.2 mm plates: four panels on corner creases (0.01 N m friction, est), eight flaps on creases sprung toward their set (0.3 N m/rad, est); bent over 3 degrees from it, a flap takes a new set there (a rule moves the spring's rest). Glue tab never peels. Panels and flaps pass through one another (real: a raised bottom flap props the top layer; one press folds both); crease angles and 12 mm thickness say flat. Board 0.55 kg/m2, friction 0.5 (est); torques: spring scale. Flats: slabs.
